notes: This row is mdxfind type MD5CAPMD5USER. CORRECTED TWICE on 2026-08-31, and the second correction matters more than the first. Waffle named the unknown vector d4f7dec5...:abc123 as the colon form, confirmed here by independent Digest::MD5 and by local mdxfind pinned to ^MD5CAPMD5USER$ with -F. But the hx specification (rev 1.15) Appendix A Note [24] then showed the stronger fact: MD5CAPMD5USER is a MULTI-EMIT type. It emits BOTH md5(cap(md5($p)).$u) and md5(cap(md5($p)).":".$u) and matches if either reproduces the stored digest. So this row is not one computation, and neither of its two vectors is anomalous -- 05b56c69... is the colonless emit and d4f7dec5... is the colon emit. The first correction here wrongly called the colonless vector foreign and removed it; it is restored. A copy also sits on md5-md5-pass-salt, which is the row for the colonless construction in its own right. john has no format for either emit: discover-john.pl ran all 957 formats against the colon vector with zero matches, and the dynamic language has no literal-string token. The 198,534-construction sweep that failed to identify this missed it because it enumerated terms and never a literal separator.

name: NETNTLMV2
notes: john reads BOTH tools' NTLMv2 serializations: measured 2026-09-01, netntlmv2 and ntlmv2-opencl load and crack this entry's hashcat-form vectors (USER::DOMAIN:challenge:response:blob) unchanged. An earlier run of this session reported "No password hashes loaded" and three re-serialized vectors were briefly added on that basis; the cause was a --field-separator-char=tab passed by the probing tool, which governs how john splits LOGIN from HASH when READING a file, so a tab made john treat each whole line as one login. The vectors were withdrawn and the tool fixed. Kerberos AS-REP is NOT like this: john genuinely cannot read hashcat's $krb5asrep$ field order, which is why those rows do carry a transcoded vector. Two reasons this block is still tier asserted, neither of which is doubt about NETNTLMv2 itself. (1) It names netlmv2, a DIFFERENT computation, and a block carries one tier for every identifier in it; netlmv2 recovers none of these vectors, and the fourth vector (aTest:::...:A1E7281FE8C10E53, an 8-byte blob far short of an NTLMv2 one) looks like the NETLMv2 one. That is a row holding two computations, which CLAUDE.md forbids, and splitting it is curation. (2) verify-vectors.pl cannot check this format at all: it writes a synthetic login and a TAB before each hash, which is right for a hash that is only a digest and wrong here, because a NETNTLMv2 ciphertext EMBEDS its own login (USER::DOMAIN:...) and john will not parse it once that field has been displaced. Measured 2026-09-01: the same vectors load and crack under netntlmv2 and ntlmv2-opencl when handed to john natively, 3 of 4, and verify-vectors.pl reports 0 of 4 for all three identifiers.

name: SHA1MD5SALTPASSPEPPER
notes: The vector here is NOT the one mdxfind's published catalog carries. mdxfind 1.543 (2026-08-29) changed what e607 computes: the old code staged the inner digest at linebuf+saltlen while writing the pepper at a fixed offset 32, so for any non-empty salt the hash covered the salt, then a TRUNCATED digest, then the pepper, and the output depended on the salt length. dlr's own note says any hash cracked as e607 before that revision will not verify against it. The catalog example 786aab530907a783e9c25a2c7326ab7907ebf798 is the PRE-FIX digest and was still being published on 2026-09-02, so it is upstream's stale artefact rather than a vector this row should carry. Replaced 2026-09-02 with the repaired construction sha1(md5(salt . pass) . pepper), established three independent ways: the source at RCS 1.545, a Digest:: recomputation in perl that reproduces 786aab... under the old layout and 0992047f... under the new, and the rebuilt binary cracking 0992047f... The salt field holds SALT then PEPPER, space separated, both 1122334455667788 here; a pepper is a site-wide secret that appears in no hash, so mdxfind reads it from a file (-j).
